To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ECM is a complex structure, produced by both cumulus cells (mainly) and oocytes, and that it may play a role in fertilization.

the extracellular matrix of the periviteline space and the surface of the ZP of mature oocytes, revealed by transmission electronmicroscopy, is composed of thin filiments and granules at interconnections of the filament which are respectively hyaluronic chains and bound proteglycans.
the ECM of porcine oocytes contains HA, that it is produced by both the oocyte and the cumulus cells, and that it is a favourable factor for fertilization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the origin, composition and presumable roles of the extracellular matrix of the porcine mature egg.
the origin, composition and presumable role of the ECM present in the PVS during oocyte maturation.
the origin and composition of the ECM of porcine oocyte and the possible role it may have on fertilization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ECM is synthesized by cumulus and oocyte cells, that it is composed of HA chains and bound proteolycans and that it is present in the perivittelline space and on both sides of ZP.
ECM of mature porcine oocytes is produced by both the cumulus and ooplasm, and that its HA moiety is a favourable factor for fertilization.
the oocyte ECM, in the PVS as well as on the ZP surface, is synthesized by both cumulus and oocyte and that its HA moiety is probably a factor favouring the penetration of spermatozoa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ECM in the PVS is a mixture of hyaluronic acids and glycoproteins, which is synthesized by both cumulus cells (and possibly the oocyte) and is probably important in sperm penetration and fertilization of the porcine mature egg.
the ECM of the porcine PVS is produced by both oocyte and corona cells and is composed of HA chains and HA bound to proteoglyphcans.
ECM in the PVS is synthesized by both oocyte and the corona cells and may play a role in sperm binding and penetration.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ECM of the porcine oocyte is not only a physical barrier to sperm penetration, but it is also a biological barrier that can be modulated to improve the in vivo fertilization of in vitro matured oocytes.
the ECM found in porcine matured oocytes is a complex structure composed of hyaluronic chains and proteoglyc can aggregates.
the oocyte and its surrounding cumulus cells contribute to the formation of an extracellular matrix (PVS) in the perivittelline space, which is composed of hyaluronic acids and glycoproteins.
